title: Fibre product in a category
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category and $a:X\to S$, $b:Y\to S$ morphisms of $\mathcal C$. A *fibre product* of $a$ and $b$ is an object $X\times_SY$ of $\mathcal C$ together with morphisms $\mathrm{pr}_1:X\times_SY\to X$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2:X\times_SY\to Y$, the *projections*, with $a\circ\mathrm{pr}_1=b\circ\mathrm{pr}_2$, such that for every object $T$ and all morphisms $x:T\to X$, $y:T\to Y$ with $a\circ x=b\circ y$ there is exactly one morphism $\varphi:T\to X\times_SY$ with $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\varphi=x$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\varphi=y$. In particular two morphisms $\varphi,\psi:T\to X\times_SY$ with $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\varphi=\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\psi$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\varphi=\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\psi$ are equal. A fibre product need not exist in a general category.
